suggestion_title: Agrupar Habilidades: Backend y DevOps Primero
suggestion_body: Clasifica tus tecnologías en categorías estratégicas: Backend & Lenguajes, Bases de Datos & Almacenamiento, DevOps & Cloud, y Frontend & UI. Priorizar Backend y DevOps primero garantiza que los filtros automáticos ATS identifiquen tu especialidad técnica en los primeros milisegundos.

suggestion_title: Formato 1 Columna: Cero Residuos de División
suggestion_body: En modo de 1 columna para ATS, elimina cualquier etiqueta o división izquierda/derecha. Los parsers ATS leen en un único flujo vertical; etiquetas divididas generan penalizaciones severas por riesgo de mezcla de texto.

suggestion_title: Orden Canónico ATS: Skills Inmediatamente tras Resumen
suggestion_body: En CVs de 1 columna optimizados para ATS, ubica las Habilidades Técnicas antes de la Experiencia Laboral para capturar el 80% de las palabras clave de la vacante en los primeros 200 tokens.

suggestion_title: Fórmula Google XYZ: Verbo de Acción + Impacto
suggestion_body: Redacta cada viñeta siguiendo 'Logré [X], medido por [Y], haciendo [Z]' (ej: 'Optimizo el rendimiento de BD mediante planes de ejecución e índices'). Evita listas de responsabilidades pasivas sin contexto de logro.

suggestion_title: Enlaces Limpios a Repositorios & Stack Explícito
suggestion_body: Incluye enlaces accesibles a repositorios GitHub o demos en vivo con su stack tecnológico explícito (ej: React, Laravel, REST APIs). Los parsers ATS y reclutadores técnicos validan código real de forma prioritaria.

Clarifica títulos académicos regionales (ej: 'Programador Universitario' con su equivalencia 'Associate Degree in Computer Programming') y estado claro ('Graduado' o 'En etapa de tesis final') para superar filtros automáticos de titulación.
Presenta Email, Teléfono, Ubicación y perfiles de LinkedIn/GitHub en texto seleccionable directo sin iconos gráficos ni tablas que bloqueen la extracción OCR del ATS.
ATS parsers read left to right, top to bottom. Tables and columns can scramble your text. Use standard left-aligned text.
Information placed in the header or footer of a document (including contact info) is often dropped entirely by ATS parsers.
ATS software cannot read text within images or graphics. Remove all photos, logos, and icons to prevent parsing errors.
Stick to common fonts like Arial, Calibri, Times New Roman, or Garamond. Unusual fonts may be converted to illegible symbols.
Use solid circle or square bullets. Fancy characters (arrows, checkmarks) may scramble the parser output.
Always use 'MM/YYYY' or 'Month YYYY' consistently (e.g., '05/2021 - Present' or 'May 2021 - August 2023'). Avoid using only years.
Use conventional titles like 'Work Experience', 'Education', and 'Skills'. ATS systems may not recognize 'Career Journey' or 'What I Do'.

suggestion_title: Include Both Acronyms and Full Terms
suggestion_body: Some ATS search for 'Search Engine Optimization', others for 'SEO'. Include both like this: 'Search Engine Optimization (SEO)'.
If your internal title was obscure (e.g., 'Happiness Engineer'), include the industry standard title as well (e.g., 'Customer Service Representative').
Include both 'Master of Business Administration' and 'MBA', or 'Bachelor of Science' and 'B.S.' so all keyword queries hit.
Format experience exactly as: Company Name, Job Title, Dates, Location. Non-standard ordering can confuse date parsing.
Text inside floating text boxes or shapes is often entirely skipped by ATS. Keep text in the main body.
Unless a PDF is explicitly requested or accepted, a standard DOCX file is the most universally accurately parsed format for legacy ATS.
A short summary packed with keywords from the target job description is a great way to boost your ATS match score early.
Empty job descriptions mean missed keyword opportunities. Detail your responsibilities focusing on hard skills and measurable outcomes.
Do not use progress bars, stars, or numerical ratings (e.g., 'Python 4/5') for skills. ATS cannot read graphics, and numbers confuse keyword counts.
Start bullet points with strong action verbs (Developed, Managed, Created). This helps ATS linguistic algorithms identify achievements.
Complex borders or horizontal lines (other than standard paragraph borders) might cause parsing to abruptly stop.
State the full name of the university, do not rely on abbreviations alone (e.g., 'Massachusetts Institute of Technology' instead of just 'MIT').
You don't need a full street address, but include City, State, and Zip Code. ATS often filters candidates by geographic location radius.
While URLs for LinkedIn or Portfolio are fine in contact info, embedding hyperlinks in regular text might break the parser. Write out the URL if necessary.
If the job asks for 'React.js', do not just write 'React'. Use the exact casing and punctuation specified in the job description.
Heavy use of italics or underlining can sometimes run characters together during OCR/parsing. Use bolding sparingly instead.
If you had multiple roles at one company, list them as separate entries with their own dates. ATS often fails to parse 'stacked' roles correctly.
Don't just dump a list of 50 skills. Ensure key skills are also mentioned in the context of your work experience bullets.
ATS systems handle 'Experience' best. Format projects with a 'Title', 'Role', and 'Dates' to ensure the parser extracts the information properly.
Avoid keyword stuffing or 'white text' tricks. Modern ATS detects this and flags the resume as spam.
If you have a university degree, omit high school. Irrelevant educational entries dilute your keyword relevance.
ATS has no fuzzy logic for typos. 'Mnagement' will not match 'Management', causing you to miss out on the keyword entirely.
Ensure current roles use present tense verbs and past roles use past tense. Advanced semantic ATS analyzers check for linguistic consistency.
Spell out 'and' instead of using '&' where possible, unless the exact company name or job requirement uses an ampersand.
ATS bots are programmed to search for hard skills (software, methodologies, licenses) much more often than soft skills (leadership, teamwork).
Do not use double spacing after periods. Multiple spaces or tabs can confuse legacy parsers into thinking a new column or section has started.
Do not write 'Spring 2019' or '2 Years'. The ATS calculates total years of experience, and needs strict months/years to do so accurately.
Put the exact title of the job you are applying for in your professional summary header. (e.g., 'Dedicated Financial Analyst').
If including GPA, format it exactly as 'GPA: 3.8/4.0'. Just writing '3.8' might not be recognized as a grade point average by the system.
Your name should be the very first line of the document on its own line, unadorned. Do not precede it with 'Resume' or 'Curriculum Vitae'.
Use standard formatting like (555) 555-5555 or 555-555-5555. Unusual formats might fail regex extraction.
Ensure the email address is plain text and professional. Sometimes ATS systems flag unprofessional emails automatically.
Instead of 'Manager/Director', write 'Manager and Director'. Some parsers will merge the word into 'ManagerDirector', destroying both keywords.
If the job asks for Angular 14, list 'Angular 14', not just 'Angular'. ATS matching is often literal.
Include quantitative data (e.g., 'Increased sales by 15%'). Some ATS look for numerical digits as a marker of strong achievements.
Omit 'Page 1 of 2' from headers or footers, as it can get mistakenly parsed as part of your experience or education.
Write out full state names or common abbreviations (e.g., 'Department' instead of 'Dept') unless explicitly abbreviated in the job listing.
Simply listing a project name isn't enough. Provide bullets detailing exactly what tools you used and your specific contribution.
Do not use 'I', 'me', or 'my'. It wastes valuable space and ATS algorithms are optimized for standard resume syntax starting with action verbs.
Keep capitalization consistent. Unpredictable casing might interfere with how an older ATS recognizes standard nouns and verbs.
Most ATS look for graduation years to calculate career length or degree completion. If left off, the degree might not be credited.
Use 'Present' or 'Current' for your current role. Using '2023' when we are in a later year suggests you are unemployed, affecting ranking.
While ATS doesn't strictly care about length, excessively long documents may hit parsing limits or time out. Keep it under 2 pages.

suggestion_title: Sintaxis Técnica ATS: Evitar Símbolos de Dólar ($N+1$, $CI/CD$)
suggestion_body: No utilices símbolos de dólar ($) para encerrar términos técnicos o fórmulas (ej: '$N+1$', '$CI/CD$'). Los parsers ATS (Workday, Taleo, Greenhouse) interpretan los signos '$' como campos salariales o variables de regex rotas, lo que provoca que las palabras clave no se indexen o se rechace el documento.

suggestion_title: Integridad de URLs: Evitar Espacios y Enlaces Temporales de Preview
suggestion_body: Verifica que ninguna URL contenga espacios en blanco accidentales y apunta siempre a dominios canónicos o repositorios definitivos en lugar de builds temporales (ej: 'deploy-preview-4...'). Los bots ATS validan la sintaxis de los enlaces y descartan URLs truncadas por espacios.

suggestion_title: Sobrecarga de Glifos: Suprimir Checkboxes (☑) y Símbolos No Estándar
suggestion_body: Suprime checkboxes (☑, ☐), tildes decorativas (✓) o caracteres gráficos en tus viñetas. Los motores de extracción de texto de los ATS transforman estos glifos en caracteres corruptos ('?', '\uFFFD') o descartan la línea completa, perdiendo los logros asociados.

suggestion_title: Taxonomía de Habilidades: Casing Canónico (JavaScript, MySQL)
suggestion_body: Escribe las tecnologías respetando su capitalización estándar de la industria (ej: 'JavaScript' en vez de 'Javascript', 'MySQL' en vez de 'mysql', 'PostgreSQL', 'Docker'). Las taxonomías de habilidades de los ATS (Lightcast, O*NET) utilizan concordancia canónica para calcular el score de afinidad técnica.
